label: AFFECTION

cover.headline: 5 small ways to *feel close again* this week
cover.sub: None of them takes more than ten minutes.

points.heading: Greet him like you mean it
points.body: When one of you walks in, stop what you’re doing for a moment. Look up, smile, say hello.

points.heading: Ten minutes, no phones
points.body: Pick a time that already exists, like after dinner. Phones face down, nothing to fix or plan.
points.panel: “Can we sit for ten minutes, just us?”

points.heading: Thank him for one specific thing
points.body: “Thanks for everything” slides right past. Something small and specific gets heard.
points.panel: “Thank you for handling school drop-off today.”

points.heading: Sit closer than usual
points.body: Same couch, same side. Closeness often starts with simply being nearby, without an agenda.
points.panel: Tonight, take the seat next to his.

points.heading: Ask one real question
points.body: Not about schedules or bills. Something you’d ask if you were still getting to know him.
points.panel: “What’s something you’ve been wanting to do?”

close.save: Save this for a week that feels far apart.

caption:
Closeness rarely disappears in one big moment. It thins out over busy weeks, one skipped hello at a time.

The way back is small, too. Pick one of these five and try it tonight. You don’t need to announce it or make it a project. Just do it and see how the evening feels.

Save this for later, and follow @spotseason for more small steps.
